market_view: CPI day. Monday was the S&P 500's best day since April (SPY +2.4% to 752.69, QQQ +3.5%, IWM +3.2%), but the rally faded late after Fed Governor Waller backed a December rate hike. At 6:45 ET futures are flat to mixed (SPY +0.1%, QQQ -0.3% pre-market), the VIX is 20, the 10-year 4.86%, WTI US$85.80 after an 11% slide in five days, gold US$4,079 and BTC US$74,200 with crypto Fear & Greed at 32. October CPI at 8:30 ET (forecast +0.3% headline, +0.2% core) decides the day, so Plan A is small and the real orders sit in Plan B and C behind price triggers. The desk's week so far: Fox +C$984 (gold long hit its target), Sam +C$40, Dax -C$25 on his first three trades.

shared_notes: CPI at 8:30 ET decides the day: Plan A is small on purpose; the option trades sit in Plan B (IWM above 284) and Plan C (IWM below 277).

New desk rules from Monday: Dax does not chase a breakout more than 0.5R past its level; a day-trade order that can no longer fill is cancelled; tickers in the plan's avoid list (Greenfire today) are refused for everyone.
Option orders go live at 9:45 ET; Vega and Theo meet at 9:31 on live quotes and can change them first.
CoreWeave reports after the close: nobody opens a new chip position into it.

day.view: Three trades on my first afternoon and I gave back C$25: BESS and TLS were bought far past their breakout levels, hours late. That is fixed: I no longer chase a break that is more than half my risk past the level. CPI at 8:30 will set the gappers, so my list builds itself at 9:45 from what opens 8% up on 3x volume and holds above VWAP. Greenfire stays off the list (takeover, in the avoid list now). Sam's and Lena's names are too big for me; I want the small caps that the CPI move wakes up.

playbook.if: a small-cap gapper (8%+, 3x volume) breaks its 15-minute high above VWAP after 9:45 and is still within 0.5R of that level
playbook.then: buy the break, stop under the range low, half off at 1R, the rest at 1.5R

playbook.if: the breakout is already more than 0.5R past its level when I see it
playbook.then: skip it: that fill sits too far from the stop the size was built on

playbook.if: a fill drops back under VWAP
playbook.then: out on the next bar; never average down

playbook.if: CPI is hot and the Russell opens down more than 1.5%
playbook.then: one clean setup at most: breakouts fail on rout mornings

playbook.if: two losers by noon
playbook.then: done for the day (rule 3a)

plan_b.note: Lunch lull, no new entries 11:30-1:30 (rule 3b): if nothing broke cleanly this morning, flat is the right answer

plan_c.note: Down 4% on the day: the tape isn't paying breakouts; stand aside

day.failsafe: Done after two losers or a 4% day loss (hard limit 6%); five trades at most; flat by 3:50 PM, no entries after 3:15.
lessons_applied: Rout mornings (S&P futures -2% or worse, VIX 25+) rarely give clean range breaks: if a hot CPI makes this one, zero or one trade is the filter working.

swing.view: I'm fully invested with C$376 of cash, so today is about managing four holdings through CPI, not buying. XERS paid half at 1R (+C$40) and rides at breakeven; MGNI closed at its 20-day high (29.04); ABNB reversed from 197.87 to close on its low (190.29), so it is the one I watch; U is fading under 52 and is first to go at 47.50. A cool CPI helps all four; a hot one tests ABNB and U first. Vega holds a U call too, so we are doubled up there: I keep my stop where it is.

playbook.if: U loses US$47.50
playbook.then: the stop sells it; no replacement buy until CPI is digested

playbook.if: MGNI makes a new high above US$29.25
playbook.then: hold for the US$31.10 target; half comes off at 1R on the way

playbook.if: ABNB loses US$186 (under Monday's low of 190.26 and the gap-day close)
playbook.then: it is next in line to be sold if a better setup needs the cash

playbook.if: XERS trades back to US$14.05
playbook.then: the breakeven stop closes the rest: the trade already paid

playbook.if: the VIX tops 26 after CPI
playbook.then: no new buys today, even if a holding stops out and frees cash

plan_b.note: U stopped at 47.50: the cash waits for Wednesday's scan; no same-day replacement on a CPI day

plan_c.note: Fear is back: no new buys; the four holdings ride their stops

swing.failsafe: No new buys above a VIX of 26; if two holdings stop out today he is done until Wednesday; the 6% day-loss limit halts him.
lessons_applied: Biggest beats hold best: XERS (the huge beat) keeps its remaining shares at breakeven while U and ABNB (smaller beats) are first in line to go.

long.view: Monday's six buys all filled and are green or flat: KLAC +9% on the day to 151.38, AAPL 350.69, plus AES, BNS, RY and Shell. I buy once a week, so the C$1,227 left stays in cash through CPI. Every stop sits about 18% under its buy price, which is far enough that a CPI wobble doesn't touch them. KLAC is still under its 50-day (174), so its 113.50 stop stays; I'm not adding into a +9% day. Sam can have the fast names.

playbook.then: no new buys this week at all

futures.view: The gold long hit its target Monday for +C$984, so I'm up 33% and I will not give it back on a CPI coin flip. Gold has since slipped to 4,079 and my trend rule already has a short waiting far below at the 20-day low (3,879). Crude is the live trade: WTI is down 11% in five days and sits at 85.80, just above Monday's low of 85.02. I sell micro crude only a quarter past that low, not on the touch. No index futures today: one micro Nasdaq contract risks too much of the book on a CPI print.

playbook.then: short 1 micro crude, stop 88.55, target 79.50

playbook.if: crude bounces above US$88.55 after the entry
playbook.then: the stop buys it back; no second try today

playbook.if: gold breaks its 20-day low (US$3,879)
playbook.then: the trend rule's short triggers with its own 2 ATR stop

playbook.if: CPI sends the dollar sharply higher
playbook.then: both shorts are with the move; still one contract each

orders.why: Micro crude short on a break of Monday's low (85.02): WTI is -11% in five days and under its 200-day (87.41); entry a quarter past the level, stop 3.80 above, target 79.50

plan_b.note: Crude short stopped at 88.55: no revenge trade; crude is done for today

plan_c.note: Down 6% on the day: no new futures; the open stops stay

futures.failsafe: One futures loss and he's done for the day; a 6% day loss stops new trades (hard limit 10%); margin rules liquidate under 90% of margin.
lessons_applied: Breaks of a level fade when the tape turns: the crude short needs 84.75, a quarter past Monday's low, not a touch of 85.02.

options_aggr.view: Both calls are under water: the NVDA 197.5 call is -18% and the U 54 call is -37%, close to its -50% stop. NVDA at 179.87 pre-market needs a real bounce, and CoreWeave tonight plus NVDA's own report on the 17th keep the premium alive. I'm not adding to either. CPI is today's trade, and I only take it after the number, in the direction the small caps pick: IWM calls above 284, IWM puts below 277, two contracts either way so a mood cut still leaves one. Theo and I meet at 9:31 on live quotes before anything goes live at 9:45.

options_safe.view: My cash is idle at C$2,998: Monday's put on American Airlines never got placed, so I'm tabling it again with CNH. Both pass my rules: AAL at US$14.16 is above its 200-day (13.47) with no report until January, and falling oil helps airlines; CNH at 12.82 is above its 200-day (11.35) after a 10.9% jump. I sell at most one cash-secured put, after CPI, and only if the VIX is under 27. Vega can have the CPI coin flip; I want the premium.

playbook.if: AAL fails but CNH holds above US$12.15

options_safe.failsafe: No put across an earnings date or on a stock under its 200-day, at most one new put a day (the limit); above a VIX of 27 he sells nothing new.
lessons_applied: Tabled two cheap quality names that pass today (AAL at US$14.16 and CNH at US$12.82, both above their 200-day), so his rules have a qualifying put instead of parked cash.

crypto.view: Bitcoin is US$74,200, sitting on its 20-day low (73,665) and just above its 200-day (73,138), with Fear & Greed at 32. I hold nine lots and only C$433 of cash, about 15% of the book, so I can afford one more add and it has to be a real flush: under US$70,000, not here. My oldest BTC lot's trailing stop is about US$72,500, so a 2% slip sells it and that is fine: it raises cash for the lower add. A hot CPI hits crypto with the Nasdaq; a cool one doesn't make me chase.

playbook.then: one add of 5% of the book, stop US$47,000: the single add this fear episode

playbook.then: the oldest lot's trailing stop sells; no re-buy above US$70,000
